breaking.headline: Three Russian missiles confirmed in Poland; NATO Council meets Monday
breaking.fact: Polish prosecutors said Sunday that all three objects that came down in southeastern Poland on Friday were Russian Kh-101 missiles, manufactured in late 2026 — and NATO’s North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels on Monday to discuss the violation. NATO chief Mark Rutte called it a grave violation; no one was hurt and Poland has not invoked Article 4.

breaking.headline: Delta outage delays 1,000+ flights as Thanksgiving travel begins
breaking.fact: A failure in Delta’s automated weight-and-balance system delayed more than 1,000 Delta flights Sunday — about half its mainline schedule — and forced a brief ground stop at Atlanta before the system was restored Sunday afternoon; Delta says about 70% of the day’s delays were the glitch, the rest bad weather in the Northeast.

weekInBrief.headline: Fifth Circuit strikes down pregnant-workers law, 9–8
weekInBrief.body: The full Fifth Circuit ruled Friday that the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act was unconstitutionally enacted because the House passed it during COVID-era proxy voting without a physical quorum, invalidating the 2022 law in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi; the ruling is expected to reach the Supreme Court.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump orders contractors to check with White House before answering Congress
weekInBrief.body: Executive Order 14438, signed Friday, requires all federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House and their agencies of any congressional request about their executive-branch work and to withhold material the White House deems privileged; noncompliance risks contract termination or suspension. Democrats call it unlawful as they prepare oversight after taking Congress in January.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump blames Democrats for a $6 trillion market slide
weekInBrief.body: In a Sunday Truth Social post, President Trump said the market has lost more than $6 trillion since Democrats’ Nov. 3 midterm wins, with the Nasdaq down 20%, and warned it “will only get worse” unless they change course; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent made a similar case on CBS. Democrats don’t take control of Congress until January.

weekInBrief.headline: Uber Eats starts drone deliveries in Spring, Texas
weekInBrief.body: Uber Eats and Zipline launched commercial drone food delivery Tuesday in Spring, a Houston suburb, with drones carrying up to eight pounds within a 10-mile radius from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.; Dallas is next, and the partners aim for dozens of U.S. cities on the way to one million drone deliveries a day by 2029.

weekendStories.headline: Aldine ISD gives away 1,000 turkeys and 10,000 pounds of produce
weekendStories.body: Aldine ISD and the Equality Health Foundation handed out 1,000 free turkeys and 10,000 pounds of fresh produce at the district’s sixth annual Healthy Fall Festival on Saturday, Nov. 21, at the M.O. Campbell Educational Center — one of a wave of Thanksgiving giveaways across Greater Houston this week.

weekendStories.headline: Rivalry food drive wraps with a 600,000-pound goal for Montana food banks
weekendStories.body: The annual Can the Cats / Can the Griz rivalry drive — Missoula and Bozeman competing to stock their local food banks — ran Nov. 7–21 with a goal of 600,000 pounds and dollars combined; the Missoula Food Bank serves one in five people in Missoula County, nearly 25,000 individuals.

weekendStories.headline: Fargo barbecue crew smokes 160 turkeys for Shriners Children’s
weekendStories.body: The El Zagal Misfits barbecue team in Fargo is smoking 160 turkeys for Thanksgiving pickup, with proceeds from the $60 birds and a turducken raffle going to Shriners Children’s; the raffle winner was drawn Nov. 19 and pickups run Thanksgiving Day at the El Zagal Shrine Temple.

weekendStories.headline: Marquette GMC sold — but keeps its name, staff and general manager
weekendStories.body: ONE Automotive Group of Eau Claire, Wisconsin, closed its purchase of Marquette GMC on Nov. 17, its first dealership in Michigan; the store keeps its name, operations and all current employees, with Nikki Remilong staying on as general manager, and the group plans a new dealership facility.

weekendStories.headline: Streams of Joy serves 600 Houston families for Thanksgiving
weekendStories.body: Streams of Joy Houston gave free turkeys to 600 families at its Joyful Tables Thanksgiving outreach on Saturday, Nov. 21, from its site on South Texas 6 — one of many volunteer-run giveaways feeding Greater Houston families ahead of Thursday’s holiday.

weekendStories.headline: 120 shelter pets fly to new lives in the Pacific Northwest
weekendStories.body: More than 50 dogs and 70 cats left Louisiana on a “Flight to Freedom” early Nov. 18, landing with shelters across the Pacific Northwest that welcomed them with open arms — many in time to find families for the holidays. Another flight is set for Dec. 1.

weekendStories.headline: Firefighters bring a missing Golden Lab home off a Virginia mountainside
weekendStories.body: Archie, a Golden Labrador missing for several days, was found stranded on a steep, wooded slope in Roanoke County’s Bent Mountain area; fire crews and animal rescuers reached him, an Angels of Assisi volunteer treated his dehydration, and he was reunited with his owner.

weekendStories.headline: A South Carolina horse rescue is named one of the state’s 2026 “Angels”
weekendStories.body: Equine Rescue of Aiken was named one of South Carolina’s 10 “Angels of 2026” on Nov. 18, an award honoring charities that put at least 80% of spending into programs; the rescue devoted 87.7% of its expenditures to helping horses, ponies and people.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A tanker sailing outbound through the strait was struck by an unidentified projectile Friday about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, catching fire with no casualties reported, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations (Warning 214-26); Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the vessel hit a naval mine, a claim not independently verified. Iran has also positioned more than 14 tankers at Kharg Island in a convoy to test the U.S. blockade, with crews assigned and flags raised, according to TankerTrackers and satellite imagery, while U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Thursday that energy flows through the strait were increasing. On oil, the roughly 200,000 barrels transferred Tuesday has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil and products kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Meet the “celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness”
space.body: Astronomers report a rare pair of extremely bright quasars — two supermassive black holes gorging on gas — shining less than a billion years after the Big Bang, a find that challenges models of how the earliest black holes grew so fast.

space.headline: Lifting weights reduces muscle loss from obesity drugs
space.body: Thrice-weekly resistance training helped middle-aged and older people keep muscle mass and strength while taking weight-loss drugs, according to research highlighted by Nature on Nov. 20 — a practical counter to one of the drugs’ main side effects.

space.headline: More tropical cyclones hit peak fury at the worst possible time
space.body: Climate change is creating conditions that pump up hurricanes’ and typhoons’ intensity just as the storms reach the coast, with more cyclones now hitting their peak at landfall, researchers report.

space.headline: Dinosaur’s rest break leaves a lasting impression
space.body: A fossilized print from Peru preserves the marks left by the feet — and the resting body — of a juvenile dinosaur about a metre tall at the hip, a rare snapshot of a young animal taking a break.

apod.title: Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3
apod.credit: Apollo 12, Alan Bean; stereo image Kevin Frank — Astronomy Picture of the Day
apod.explanation: Put on your red/blue glasses and gaze across the western Ocean of Storms on the Moon. The 3D anaglyph shows Apollo 12 astronaut Pete Conrad visiting the Surveyor 3 spacecraft in November 1969; Surveyor 3 had landed at the site in April 1967, and Apollo 12’s Lunar Module Intrepid touched down less than 200 meters (650 feet) away. The stereo image was created from two photos taken from only slightly different viewpoints, approximating the separation between human eyes.

aiModels.notes: The pick to beat — purpose-built for Spark-class boxes: ~24GB footprint, ~84 tok/s reported, hits the 256K context target.

aiModels.run: vLLM / SGLang / llama.cpp (GGUF); Ollama on Apple silicon only at launch
aiModels.notes: Frontier-class agent scores on vendor benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified 79.2%, unverified); early Spark hands-ons show 40–76 tok/s, but most tokens burn on hidden reasoning.

aiModels.run: vLLM / SGLang (WSL2 on Windows); community GGUF
aiModels.notes: The deep-think option from the project's Nov 20 checkpoint: strongest US-open agentic benchmarks and up-to-1M context, but ~80GB and a Linux/WSL2 serving path.
The turnkey option: maker-documented Ollama path, Apache 2.0, fast on mini hardware (~60 tok/s class) — but 128K context sits exactly at the project floor, and it is text-only.

aiHardware.notes: The frontrunner — the only box ticking every project criterion today: CUDA, Windows-native, Microsoft support, shipping now. Bolt-class models run ~84 tok/s on this silicon. Ceiling: 128GB is learning-class; it cannot touch Spark Open itself.
Most memory in a mini — room for the 120B deep-think brain plus a fat 256K KV cache. No CUDA (ROCm/Vulkan serving), you assemble it yourself, and batches sell out.
Cheapest US-company route to a 128GB Windows box. The shortage in one row: launched at $1,999 in Jul 2025, now $4,700 — and Windows caps its GPU memory at 96GB.

readiness.headline: Close — the box exists and the speed is there; the brain is one tier shy — projected to be at 100% around Q4-2028
readiness.lacking: A local model at hosted-Muse tier (today's best stack is a strong supervised junior) · Spark-Open-class capability needs a ~700GB box — the DGX Station class, whose Windows price is still unannounced · memory-shortage prices are still rising, so waiting keeps earning points · Windows serving paths for the favorite models are proven on paper, not yet hands-on
readiness.today: $5,999 → Surface Dev Box + Bolt 74B always-on (~84 tok/s) + Super 120B for deep think = a working local agent at 76/100. The experience today: about half the capability of hosted Muse — chat at full speed, deep thinking at about half pace. A strong junior on the desk, not a replica.
